event.description: Tie the final LayerNorm scale to the shared first pre-attention LayerNorm scale while retaining layer-shared attention outputs, no offsets, rank-4 tied tokens, factorized rank-3 positions, d=14, ff=19, and the 75000-step schedule.
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Retained incumbent is attempt-0058 with 2690 parameters at 99.940000%, a +0.940000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the most recent accepted result is attempt-0058, cross-layer attention-output sharing (2690, 99.94%); the most recent failed result is attempt-0049, multi-query attention, an optimization failure; 10 prior parameter-tying macro attempts. The preceding rank-3 token automation failure establishes a token-rank boundary but does not test final normalization calibration. Hypothesis: after tying the corresponding pre-norms across blocks, the final norm's learned scale may encode the same residual-stream calibration as the shared first pre-attention norm. This is a parameter-tying representational change, not scalar pruning: it shares one 14-scalar scale vector while retaining the final normalization operation and all normalization statistics, reducing actual parameters from 2690 to 2676. It is more informative than retrying the previously failed final-to-pre-FF tie because it isolates a different, role-closer pre-attention normalization scale in the materially changed, attention-output-tied architecture.
